title: Finite polynomial subalgebra extension containing scaled generators
statement: For an injective algebra map from a domain R to a commutative ring S, and a finite set g generating S as an R-algebra, there exist d, coordinates y in S, a subalgebra S' containing the injective polynomial evaluation range R[y], and a nonzero f in R, such that S' is finite over R[y] through the inclusion and f*x belongs to S' for every x in g. No localization conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: Localize S at the images of the nonzero elements of R. The localization is nontrivial because R → S is injective. Its K-algebra is generated by the images of g, where K is FractionRing R: a localized numerator belongs to their adjoin and its denominator is a unit coming from K. Apply field Noether normalization. Lift each coordinate after multiplication by an individual nonzero denominator to t_i in S. Scaling variables by these units is an automorphism of K[T], so the resulting evaluation is still finite and injective. Its composition with R[T] → K[T] equals R[T] → S → S_K. Injectivity of R[T] → K[T] and of the K-evaluation proves injectivity of evaluation in S.

Give S its R[T]-algebra structure through evaluation at t. Finiteness makes every element in S_K integral over K[T]. IsIntegral.exists_multiple_integral_of_isLocalization clears coefficient denominators; IsLocalization.exists_isIntegral_smul_of_isIntegral_map clears the localization-zero relation. Together these produce, for each x in S, a nonzero scalar c(x) such that c(x)*x is integral over R[T]. Let f be the product of c(x) over g. It is nonzero, and c(x) divides f for x in g. Multiplying c(x)*x by the remaining scalar preserves integrality, so f*x is integral over R[T].

Let E be the R-polynomial evaluation range in S. Restrict the evaluation codomain to E to form the tower R[T] → E → S. Integrality over R[T] implies integrality over E. Construct U as the E-subalgebra of S generated by the finite image of g under x ↦ f*x. The finite-integral-adjoin theorem makes U a finite E-module. Define S' by restricting U to R. The inclusion E → S' is the same algebra structure on its underlying subtype, so it has this finite-module instance. E is contained in S' because an E-subalgebra contains its scalars, and every f*x lies in S' by subset_adjoin.

theorem exists_finite_subalgebra_away_core
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (g : Finset S) (hgen : Algebra.adjoin R (g : Set S) = ⊤) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (y : Fin d → S) (S' : Subalgebra R S),
      Function.Injective (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) y) ∧
      ∃ h : (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) y).range ≤ S',
        (letI := (Subalgebra.inclusion h).toRingHom.toAlgebra
         Module.Finite (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := R) y).range S') ∧
        ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ g, algebraMap R S f * x ∈ S'
